problems: Compiler behaviour for the orchestrator: a `merge` event whose counterpart has no dossier is applied as the state releasing its own land to nobody when it holds at least as many cells as are free (compile_dossiers.py merge()); other dossiers with such merges after a found event may show the same large keyframe snap. The one in russian-state is fixed here.

Compiler behaviour: a one-year keyframe is compared with the ledger at the end of its start year, so keyframes that describe a mid-year peak or the date of proclamation (russian-state_1919, people-s-republic-of-china_1949) always snap; I corrected those two to year-end shapes.

No compile was run (not mine to run): effects are reasoned from the compiler code, the draft windows in compiled/_draft and set arithmetic with the gazetteer; the orchestrator's next run should confirm the snaps shrink to the residuals named in the notes (russian-state_1919 about 144 cells, tsardom-of-russia_1653 about 1,458, RSFSR_1919 Volgograd/Crimea/Belarus about 800, RSFSR_1918 Tuva/Navoi overdraw, PRC_1949 about 1,000).
The gazetteer README says {minus:[A,B,...]} subtracts all later items, but dossier.schema.json allows exactly two items in a minus; I used two-item minus with a union as the second.
